created.title: perf(setup): stream OpenCode token usage rows
created.body:
## Problem

Setup counts OpenCode usage by materializing every assistant token payload with SQLite `.all()` before adding the counters. A long-running agent history therefore consumes memory proportional to all of its messages, although only one row's counters and the earliest timestamp are needed at a time.

## Change

Consume the same query through the existing `streamRows` helper, using SQLite's iterator on supported Bun versions and preserving the established `.all()` fallback on older runtimes. V1/V2 selection, migrated-ID deduplication, the usage window, counter interpretation and read-only database lifetime stay the same.

## Measurement

A real on-disk SQLite fixture containing 300,000 assistant messages (input 50, output 5, reasoning 5, cache read 40, plus a 300-character unused token field) was scanned in fresh Bun 1.4.4 processes on Linux. All six runs returned exactly 30,000,000 tokens and zero skipped sources.

| Version | Peak RSS across three runs | Median scan time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unchanged main | 272–277 MiB | 723 ms |
| Streaming | 48–53 MiB | 507 ms |

The median peak memory fell from 274 MiB to 50 MiB (about 82%). These are local fixture measurements, not a claim about every machine or transcript size.

## Validation

- The full prompt-import selection completed 146 tests and had four setup test timeouts during concurrent machine load.
- Re-ran all four directly relevant files (setup scan, token usage, OpenCode V2 history, and WAL window) with a 30-second test timeout: **33 passed, 0 failed, 142 assertions**, finishing in 1.51 seconds. This includes the previously timed-out cases.
- Follow-up compatibility check: token usage, OpenCode history/WAL, and the existing streaming-helper fallback suites pass (**21 tests, 87 assertions**). Root TypeScript and all bundle targets pass again after using `streamRows`.
- Root and viewer TypeScript checks pass.
- All bundle targets and distribution checks pass via `node scripts/build-hooks.js`; generated output is not included. Dependency-lock regeneration was not run because dependencies are unchanged.
- `git diff --check` passes.

## Related history

Checked all 3,210 historical PR records and the full commit history for this source file. #5788 introduced the current OpenCode table selection and migration deduplication; this change bounds the memory needed to consume that selection. It is separate from the pending Codex counter correction in #5886.

created.title: fix(parser): preserve closing tags inside XML literals
created.body:
## Problem

An observer can describe XML in a CDATA section, for example a narrative containing `</observation>`. The parser currently treats that literal as the record terminator, silently truncates the saved narrative, and drops the fields that follow it. The same issue affects summary fields and fact arrays. A commented document example can also be selected ahead of the actual reply.

## Change

Mask angle brackets inside CDATA sections and XML comments while matching the reply's structure. Recover field contents from the original text using the unchanged offsets, preserving the existing CDATA/entity storage behavior. Apply the same masking to the unfinished-observation check so a literal closing tag cannot complete a truncated response. Document this parsing boundary in the observer lifecycle notes.

## Validation

- Five regression cases fail on the base commit: observation truncation, summary truncation, array truncation, commented examples, and unfinished CDATA.
- Parser, character-reference, and response-processor suites: **112 passed, 424 assertions**. The new observation regression also stores and reads the parsed content through the real SQLite SessionStore.
- Media observation-turn integration suite: **51 passed, 306 assertions**, covering attachment parsing and linkage.
- Root and viewer TypeScript checks passed.
- `node scripts/build-hooks.js`: all bundle targets and distribution checks passed.

Based on current main `6b779c06796138aeb4b0ee2fa7dbd25912e4f7fb`. Checked the parser's commit history and all historical PR titles/bodies: this addresses structural matching of literal markup, distinct from character-reference decoding (#4360), skip dispatch inside an already-selected document (#5702), and nested-field matching (#835).

## CI matrix follow-up

The sync-api matrix job remains failed at `scripts/sync-matrix-e2e.ts:598`: `review fingerprints agree across distinct replica ids` ([job log](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/actions/runs/43000892066/job/130456439523)). To check whether this patch introduced it, I ran the unmodified `bun scripts/sync-matrix-e2e.ts` twice in the same Linux environment with Bun 1.4.4 and PostgreSQL 16.15, recreating the database and using a separate empty data directory for each run. Both upstream main `6b779c06796138aeb4b0ee2fa7dbd25912e4f7fb` and this PR's source at `4e9f3466b9bb5591669e1f27410033001ae00e4c` fail at that same assertion after the shared group membership and 60 percent progress check passes. This reproduces the failure on the existing base; it does not turn the failed CI check into a pass. The other nine substantive CI checks passed.

Upstream investigation [#6007](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues/6007) also cites this matrix run and identifies a shared-activity publication failure: after a transient SQLite writer lock, the reconciler advances its capture cache despite the failed publication. The existing, still-open fix [#5870](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/pull/5870) addresses that ordering and signature-cache path. Its regression holds a writer lock on a second real SQLite connection, rolls it back without changing `data_version`, then verifies that the next ordinary reconcile publishes provenance, transfers the linked work to another store, and does not add duplicate records on another unchanged pass. That sync fix is separate from this parser patch. The original failed matrix check above remains failed; neither this link nor the independent reproduction changes its status.

created.title: fix(sqlite): retain distinct structured observation content
created.body:
## Problem

Exact observation deduplication hashes only the session, title, and narrative. Two valid observations with the same title and no narrative but different facts therefore return the same ID; the second fact is never stored or searchable. Different subtitles, types, and concepts are affected as well, including exact-only authored saves with title deduplication bypassed.

## Change

Keep the existing fingerprint and row for compatible historical retries. When that fingerprint is occupied by different structured content, store the other content under a deterministic details fingerprint. Stored JSON arrays and input arrays compare consistently, including imported JSON with different whitespace.

Check a details fingerprint before selecting a free legacy fingerprint, so deleting the original variant cannot duplicate a retained variant on replay. Run the identity reads and writes under the existing transaction's immediate writer lock. Optional normalized-title merging still follows its configured policy, while tool-derived file evidence and agent/media metadata keep their existing provenance/linkage behavior.

## Validation

- **All 7 new regressions fail on unchanged main.**
- **133 tests passed, 634 assertions** across SQLite deduplication/migration, reinforcement, response processing, and real media observation-turn integration.
- The new tests verify persisted facts through actual SQLite FTS recall, mixed-batch retries, legacy hash/ID preservation, exact-only authored saves, optional title merging, and replay after deleting the original variant.
- Root and viewer TypeScript checks passed.
- All bundle targets and distribution checks passed with `node scripts/build-hooks.js`; generated artifacts are not included.
- `git diff --check` passed.

created.title: fix(context): count persisted facts once in token estimates
created.body:
## Problem

The context and setup token-economics paths receive `facts` as JSON text from SQLite. The calculator serializes that string again, so every stored quote and backslash gains another escape layer in the read-cost estimate. NULL facts also contribute an invented `[]`. Both the per-observation read cost and the aggregate savings are affected.

For a real stored observation with a four-character title, eight-character narrative, and 29-character facts JSON containing a quoted value and a Windows path, the existing four-characters-per-token estimate should be 11. The current implementation reports 14. A legacy row with NULL facts and the same title/narrative reports 4 instead of 3.

## Change

Count the persisted facts text directly, just like the other stored text fields, and let missing fields contribute zero. Keep the existing estimate and per-observation rounding. Update the calculator and rendered-cost expectations and document how the estimate is formed.

## Validation

- Both new regressions fail on unchanged main.

created.title: perf(import): assemble long transcript lines once
created.body:
## Problem

The shared JSONL reader appends each 1 MiB chunk to an unfinished line, then searches the whole accumulated string again. A large assistant/tool record repeatedly copies and scans its earlier chunks. Setup's prompt and token-history readers all use this path.

## Change

Find newlines within each decoded chunk and retain only unfinished line fragments. Join the fragments once when their line ends, or once at EOF. The stream still provides UTF-8 decoding, errors still propagate, and empty lines, CRLF text and a final line without a newline retain their existing behavior. No records are truncated or skipped.

## Measurement

A real 33,554,483-byte JSONL fixture contains one 32 MiB payload record between two small records, with no final newline. Each fresh Bun 1.4.4 process reads it through the production `readLines` export and hashes every returned line. All six runs produce the same 3 lines, 33,554,481 content characters and SHA-256 digest.

| Version | Three read-and-hash times | Median peak RSS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unchanged main | 344, 256, 272 ms | 199 MiB |
| Fragment assembly | 179, 123, 124 ms | 140 MiB |

The local fixture's median time falls from 272 to 124 ms and median peak memory by about 30%. This measures the line reader with hashing, not an entire setup run or model workload.

## Validation

- Eight new filesystem cases cover empty files/records, CRLF, multi-chunk records between small records, an unterminated large final record, a UTF-8 code point crossing the read window, and read-error propagation.
- All prompt-import suites: 158 passed, 0 failed, 377 assertions across 21 files, including the existing partial-read and fork-history cases.
- Root and viewer TypeScript checks pass.
- `node scripts/build-hooks.js` passes for every bundle target and distribution checks. Generated bundles are not included. Dependencies are unchanged; plugin dependency-lock regeneration was not run.
- `git diff --check` passes.

created.title: fix(memory): decode quoted native note metadata
created.body:
## Problem

Native Markdown notes can use valid quoted YAML metadata, but the importer only removes the outer quote marks. A name such as `'Don''t forget "cache"'` is stored with two apostrophes, and escaped quotes, backslashes or Unicode characters remain encoded in descriptions and metadata. Escaped `metadata.type` values also produce incorrect searchable concept tags.

## Change

Decode single-line quoted values for the parser's existing known keys: doubled apostrophes in single-quoted scalars, and YAML named/hexadecimal escapes in double-quoted scalars. Decode once, so an escaped backslash cannot become a second escape. Unknown, malformed and invalid-code-point sequences remain literal. Plain values and Markdown prose retain their existing interpretation.

The implementation stays within the existing small frontmatter parser; no YAML dependency or multiline-scalar support is added. The rules follow [YAML 1.2.2 escaped characters](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#57-escaped-characters) and [single-quoted style](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#732-single-quoted-style).

## Validation

- The final new regression suite on unchanged main: **5 failed, 2 passed**.
- Actual LF and CRLF Markdown files pass through `ingestMemorySource` and `SessionStore`; persisted title, subtitle, searchable concepts and provenance now contain decoded text, while the narrative remains literal.
- Existing ingestion and Unicode preview suites plus the new cases: **36 passed, 0 failed, 103 assertions**.
- Controls cover one-pass decoding, single-quoted backslashes, malformed escapes and unquoted/incomplete values.
- Root and viewer TypeScript checks pass.
- `node scripts/build-hooks.js` passes for all bundle targets and distribution checks. Generated bundles are not included. Dependencies are unchanged; plugin dependency-lock regeneration was not run.

created.title: fix(import): retain Unicode in prompt provenance
created.body:
## Problem

Prompt provenance normalization discards every letter outside `a-z`. A long Chinese, Japanese, Arabic or Cyrillic instruction copied from an earlier agent output therefore bypasses the authorship check and is imported as the owner's request. ## Change

Preserve Unicode letters and numbers in both the TypeScript importer and the Python owner-goals export. Count the existing 160-character threshold and 120-character fingerprint in code points, and roll the streaming hash over code points while retaining string offsets for exact collision verification. The lowercase-opening rule recognizes supplementary alphabets and other Unicode lowercase characters as Python does. Temporal checks and role-assignment handling retain their existing policy.

created.title: fix(projects): retain recall through repeated project merges
created.body:
## Problem

Three successive whole-project merges (`repo/feature → repo → work → portfolio`) leave the original worktree's saved observations and summaries on disk but omit them from the final project's SessionStart context, search and file history. Read-key expansion discovers only immediate merged sources; the per-row alias predicate supplies just one additional hop.

## Change

Expand whole-project read keys to a fixed point, retaining the existing rule that every observation and summary of a promoted source must be adopted into known destinations. Partially adopted projects still contribute only their adopted rows. Follow the complete chain within one read transaction, retain literal spellings for semantic search, and use SQLite's ASCII-only case equivalence to terminate without re-querying case variants. Each pass keeps the existing covering-index queries and finalizes its statement.

Stored project names, merge stamps and sync operations are unchanged. Existing partial-adoption protections from #4789 and large-catalog bind reuse from #5549 remain in place.

## Validation

- Five of seven new regressions fail on unchanged main `6b779c0`; both scope/write controls pass.

- Additional coverage verifies reachable/disconnected cycles, case variants, and a whole source split across destinations discovered at different depths.

created.title: perf(telemetry): aggregate event statistics on arrival
created.body:
## Problem

The telemetry buffer retains every context-injection and observer-turn property object until its session/window flush, then walks all those records on the worker event loop. Its memory and flush cost grow with the number of events between flushes, although the emitted result needs only totals, sample counts, frequencies and last-seen source fields.

## Change

Accumulate those statistics when each event arrives. Keep the existing per-session observer rollups and separate five-minute context window, including emission timing, safety-flush thresholds/sequences, finite-sample average denominators, first-seen frequency ties and last nonempty source values. Reset all statistics when a window is rearmed. No provider, inference queue, consent, whitelist or network-send behavior changes.

Retained state scales with active sessions and distinct model/reason values, rather than event count. Add a reproducible local benchmark whose telemetry sink is replaced so it sends no metrics.

## Measurement

`bun scripts/bench-telemetry-buffer.ts 200000` records a synthetic burst of 200,000 context events and 200,000 observer turns across 64 sessions, then drains the existing flush paths. On Bun 1.4.4/Linux, medians of three separate processes per revision:

| Metric | Main `6b779c0` | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained heap after collection | 49.51 MiB | 0.18 MiB |
| Peak RSS | 91.64 MiB | 41.86 MiB |
| Record + flush time | 126.46 ms | 37.92 ms |
| Flush time | 68.91 ms | 0.81 ms |

All six runs emit the same 65 rollups with the same full-payload SHA-256 (`5744788b5e9ee8742e5ea9d1e1c9927d600d7643d9665f04eebf2edbe0b4eded`). The explicit collection used to measure retained heap is excluded from record/flush timing.

## Problem

Long memory questions (at least 600 characters) can lose observations and summaries that a direct keyword search finds. created.title: fix(import): retain compressed Codex history
created.body:
## Problem

Native Codex compresses cold rollouts after seven days to `.jsonl.zst`, retaining their modification time and removing the plain file. The prompt import locator accepts only `.jsonl`, so these files disappear from the existing 30-day scan. - Discover compressed rollouts in the existing dated session folders. Follow Codex's plain-sibling precedence while both files exist, preventing stale prompts and duplicated usage.
- Stream Zstandard bytes into the existing UTF-8 line reader. Reuse the existing frame-header scanner before decoding because Bun's streaming decoder can otherwise finish a truncated frame without an error. Native Codex's verified single-frame format remains streamed; no decompressed copy is written to disk.
- Retain the same filename-based session identity after compression when a legacy header has no ID.
- Look up the codec at call time. A missing codec, damaged frame or input read failure reaches the existing skipped-source reporting path; ordinary files remain readable.

created.title: fix(work-view): checkpoint bounded initial owner-goals mapping
created.body:
Fixes #5969.

A large first My Work goals refresh currently sends the entire owner-prompt window in one question. If a later quote check fails, no snapshot exists and the next refresh repeats the whole window. A synthetic 5,922-prompt regression reproduces a 1,937,206-byte API question on current main.

This change maps large initial windows in batches, carrying forward only checked cumulative goals:

- Each prompt batch is at most 32 KiB; the complete question, including instructions, focus areas, the carried draft and any refused answer, is limited to 96 KiB of UTF-8. Every exported source turn remains covered.
- An atomic checkpoint pairs the checked draft with exact source identities/content hashes. Same-minute additions, edits, equal text in different turns, and deletion followed by restoration are distinct. Completed, unchanged batches are reused after interruption.
- Every new cumulative answer uses the existing strict Python quote validator against the complete current window and the focus route's preflight. A batch with no actionable goals can carry `null` before any snapshot exists; it does not save an unsupported empty snapshot or discard a nonempty draft.
- A payload-bound focus save key gives interrupted final saves stable, owner/device-scoped area IDs. Retries preserve owner renames, dismissal and merges, reread current rules, and advance `generated_at` only after items and rules are saved.
- Final retries revalidate current source evidence before local outputs and worker writes. Invalid evidence or validator-induced changes refuse the saved payload without another model call. Cached map prose is explicitly an unverified audit trail and is discarded when its source changes.

The recovery contract is documented in `docs/architecture/owner-goals-refresh.md`. The separate HTTP writes are retried idempotently; they are not a cross-store transaction, and snapshot preflight is not an atomic cross-process compare-and-set. Initial mapping uses more, smaller requests; token totals depend on the carried draft. The existing refresh entry points and selected agent still determine when inference runs.

### Validation

The model answers in these tests are deterministic; Python validation/saving, HTTP requests, SQLite projections and focus routes are real.

- [Current-main negative control and incremental-update control](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43033746489/job/130567094026): the 5,922-prompt case fails on the actual oversized question; the existing incremental update passes.

## Changes

Use OpenCode's own activity boundary: a fork message belongs to the fork's new activity only when `message.time_created >= session.time_created`.

- Apply that boundary to V2 owner prompts and token usage when the native session table has both `fork_session_id` and `time_created`.
- Retain activity exactly at the boundary, including a genuinely new request whose text matches an earlier request. No text-based deduplication is introduced.
- Retain inherited assistant text for authorship checking, including a retained fork whose parent session was deleted.
- Preserve non-fork and subagent token accounting, and the existing behavior of older V2 snapshots without the fork columns.

Smart-read omits explicit TypeScript `declare function` declarations, including the `export declare function` form used in generated `.d.ts` APIs. The native grammar represents these as an `ambient_declaration` around a `function_signature`; the existing query only captures implemented `function_declaration` nodes. A declaration-only function therefore has no outline entry, cannot be found by native symbol search, and cannot be unfolded by name.

The shape is defined by [tree-sitter-typescript's grammar](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-typescript/blob/v0.23.2/common/define-grammar.js).

## Changes

Capture explicit declared functions in the TypeScript/TSX query and retain their native source ranges, names, export flags and documentation. Read the complete native declaration as its signature, keeping multiline parameters and object return types through the semicolon within the existing 200-character budget.

The JavaScript query stays valid for its separate grammar. Ordinary TypeScript overload signatures are outside this capture, so they do not shadow an existing implementation when unfolding it. This patch covers explicit `declare function` syntax; it does not claim support for all implicit ambient declarations or all overload representations.

## Validation

Base: `308a9ab4a141ac49ca0e72bbccc0c9cdf3770ca0`.
Head: `70b86c2591eaac1db465ec97587fed16812b0179`.

[Fixed-SHA comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43047191406), Bun 1.4.4 / Node 20 / native Tree-sitter CLI 0.26.13:

- [Fixed head](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43047191406/job/130614171507): **6 pass / 33 assertions**.
- The complete smart-file-read directory, including the new cases: **283 pass / 950 assertions across 62 files**.
- Root and viewer TypeScript, every shipped bundle target, test-lane ownership and `git diff --check` pass.

The tests run the production parser with actual native grammars, the native batch search path against owned files, and `unfoldSymbol`. They cover `.d.ts`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, exported/local declarations, documentation, multiline generic/object types, namespace-qualified identities, implemented overloads and plain JavaScript. A missing native CLI fails CI explicitly.

## History check

Checked all-state/all-author searches for `function_signature`, `declare function`, ambient declarations and TypeScript signatures. #4994 handles abstract classes/methods, #5006 handles namespace containers, and #4480 handles interface ownership; those changes do not expose explicit declared functions.

The original [upstream typecheck/build/test job](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/actions/runs/43048411026/job/130618543415) remains failed. Its first failure is the Fish/ripgrep/xsel installation: APT cannot resolve `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` and exits 100. ## Problem

A Claude result can backfill `discovery_tokens` after its assistant frame has already stored observations and a context block has been cached. `updateDiscoveryTokens` corrects SQLite and marks changed rows for sync, but does not notify the context cache. The agent's full-observation label and the human timeline therefore keep the initial token count while a fresh render shows the completed usage.

The regression records 40 tokens, caches the actual context, then corrects the same observation to 4,096. Unchanged main continues serving 40 in all three affected cases: agent output, human output and a partially adopted observation under another project.

## Changes

Collect the affected project keys from observation rows whose stored usage actually changes, then emit one existing context-invalidation event after the transaction commits. Include both the original project and `merged_into_project`: a partial adoption intentionally does not promote its whole source project into the recipient's read scope.

Keep no-op and missing-ID updates out of the render queue, deduplicate repeated IDs/project keys, and do not emit if the transaction rolls back. Summary-only corrections retain their existing monotonic update behavior without scheduling an observation-label render.

created.title: perf(viewer): bound legacy prompt retry lookups by time
created.body:
## Problem

The prompt feed checks each legacy prompt for a later same-text retry in its session. Its current time-difference predicate cannot constrain the lookup index by time, so a long session repeatedly scans its full history before ordering and paginating the result. These are synchronous SQLite reads on the worker.

## Change

- Express the existing inclusive ten-second window as a bounded timestamp range.
- Add a partial `(session_db_id, created_at_epoch)` index for legacy rows with no native prompt ID. It indexes timestamps rather than copying prompt text.
- Keep the existing newest-timestamp/newest-ID rule, distinct native turns, project/platform/session scope, and pagination behavior.
- Cover the actual production query and reopen an existing database. The older native-identity migration fixture also removes the new dependent index before simulating a table without `native_prompt_id`.

## Measured effect

[Same-runner comparison](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43053026084/job/130634984470), Bun 1.4.4 on Linux: each revision opens a separate owned SQLite database with **12,000 distinct legacy prompts in one session**, spaced five seconds apart. The benchmark calls the actual `PaginationHelper.getPrompts()`, warms each page once, then measures five reads. Database setup is outside the query timings.

| Page, 50 rows | Main median (range), ms | Fixed median (range), ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First page | 15,271.95 (15,236.78–15,447.10) | 19.04 (18.12–19.79) |
| Offset 6,000 | 15,197.70 (15,133.83–15,469.37) | 24.05 (23.34–27.84) |

Both complete returned page objects have identical SHA-256 hashes across revisions:
- First page: `809e4086b6e13e5cc4450d1819865655e4b95c9ff6d5e7b692162aba6d8ce6fc`
- Offset 6,000: `244a2e6427a93d76de85ff64d8c92c8a1281004368e00c06431e16b4ebf7b45c`

The query plan changes from a session-only lookup to a session lookup bounded by both timestamp endpoints. These timings describe this concentrated-session fixture, not every history distribution. The log also records insertion and existing-database reopen times; the new index has a write/storage cost.

<details>
<summary>All five query measurements, in milliseconds</summary>

- Main, first page: 15447.10, 15271.95, 15266.46, 15306.97, 15236.78
- Fixed, first page: 19.36, 19.79, 18.51, 18.12, 19.04
- Main, offset 6,000: 15133.83, 15469.37, 15282.86, 15197.70, 15173.63
- Fixed, offset 6,000: 24.05, 25.01, 23.64, 27.84, 23.34

</details>

## Validation

Final head: `7487cc5d29d2b7f7fed598999e2704e0ec9b74ea`, based on `308a9ab4a141ac49ca0e72bbccc0c9cdf3770ca0`.

- On unchanged main with the new tests (`ef0051e57af8cbea0160b13a47bf0bee2706e94d`), all **four semantic groups pass**; only the test requiring a bounded lookup in the actual SQLite query plan fails. This is a query-performance change, not a change to which prompts are visible.
- [Final gates](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43054777484/job/130641177988): **5 focused tests / 17 assertions**, **33 related tests / 179 assertions**, root and viewer TypeScript, all shipped bundles, test-lane coverage, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Boundaries include retries at 9,999, 10,000 and 10,001 ms, equal timestamps, native IDs, page boundaries and independent session/platform/project scopes.
- The first comparison run passed the benchmark and all new regressions, then an existing migration fixture failed while dropping a column still referenced by the new index (**32 related passes, 1 failure**). The final fixture removes that index as part of restoring the old schema. The final job verifies production bytes are identical to measured implementation `864dd004`; the new regression's child also has a verified 20-second deadline.

History checked: #2515 added retry deduplication, #4747 fixed feed ordering, and #4748 preserved native prompt identities. This keeps those contracts while bounding the legacy retry lookup.

created.title: fix(smart-read): include compact Java record constructors
created.body:
## Problem

A Java record's compact constructor has no explicit parameter list in its declaration. Tree-sitter represents it as `compact_constructor_declaration`, which the Java symbol query does not capture. As a result, smart outline, search, and unfold omit the body that validates or normalizes record components, even while showing an explicit constructor overload and nearby methods.

## Change

Capture a compact constructor directly inside its owning record body and pair it with that record header's formal parameters. Reuse the existing constructor identity, method classification, source range, signature, and owner handling.

For example, `record Range(int low, int high) { public Range { ... } }` now exposes `Range.Range(int low, int high)` for exact unfolding. Its displayed signature remains the source declaration `public Range`; its body range does not include the record header or other methods.

The grammar distinguishes this node from ordinary constructors: [tree-sitter-java v0.23.5](https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-java/blob/v0.23.5/grammar.js). The implicit parameters come from the record header, including variable arity, as specified by [JLS 17 §8.10.4.2](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se17/html/jls-8.html#jls-8.10.4.2).

## Validation

[Fixed-SHA native comparison and complete gates](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43056678576/job/130647862368), Bun 1.4.4, actual Tree-sitter CLI 0.26.13 and javac 17.0.21:

- The checked-in fixture compiles with `javac --release 17`.
- Unchanged main `308a9ab` plus these tests (`8a82b1e`): **5 fail, 1 pass**, 9 assertions. Compact-constructor outline/search/unfold cases fail; ordinary and explicit canonical constructors pass.
- Fixed head `2016191510990e8f599c72f2b1af9a68dd29cfde`: **6 pass, 27 assertions**. Cases cover exact body bounds, source signature and documentation, an overload, nested record ownership, generic/multiline/varargs headers, an empty component list, and native batched search followed by qualified unfolding.
- Entire `tests/services/smart-file-read` suite: **283 pass, 944 assertions across 62 files**, including the six new cases.
- Root and viewer TypeScript checks, all shipped bundles, test-lane ownership, and `git diff --check` pass. Existing advisory bundle-size warnings remain visible in the log.

The earlier ordinary-constructor work in #4439 and record-container work in #4496 do not capture this distinct compact-constructor node; both behaviors are retained by the controls.
